lessons.notes:
Why most beginners lose money

In Europe, every regulated broker must show on its website how many of its ordinary (retail) clients lose money trading CFDs such as forex and Gold. When the European regulator ESMA reviewed these numbers in 2018, they ranged from 74% to 89% of retail accounts losing money. So the useful question is not why so many people lose. It is: what do the people who survive do differently? This lesson answers that question and gives you the full map of the free course.

The biggest beginner mistake: the wrong order

Most beginners watch a strategy in some video, open an account and deposit money. That is like building the roof of a house before the foundation. They cannot calculate a pip, do not know lot size and do not understand leverage. Every professional trader knows that the real difference comes less from the strategy and more from risk management and discipline. The problem is not intelligence. It is the order.

Who this course is for

  • People who know nothing about forex.
  • People who have traded, lost money, and now want to learn the basics properly.

It is for viewers in Pakistan and India, in simple Urdu/Hindi, with English subtitles on every video and written notes on this website.

Two traders, same strategy: why risk decides who survives

Two traders use exactly the same strategy with a $1,000 account. The first risks 10% of his balance on every trade, the second only 1%. Both get five losses in a row, which can happen to any strategy.

The first account is down 41% and now needs a 69% profit just to get back to $1,000. The second is down only about 5% and needs about 5%. Same strategy, completely different result. That is the answer to the opening question: the people who survive learn in the right order and control their risk on every trade. Module 8 shows how to find the right lot size from your stop loss, and you can try it now with the free lot size calculator.

How to use this course: 4 rules

  1. Watch the lessons in order. Each lesson builds on the one before.
  2. Read the notes. The notes for every lesson are free on qaziforextips.com. Read them after the video.
  3. Do the 10-minute practical task. Trading is learned by doing, not by watching.
  4. No real money until the basics are complete. First learn, then demo, then small money.

What this course is not

You will not get signals here, there is no promise of guaranteed profit, and we do not promote any broker. Forex laws are different in every country, so check your own country's rules (see forex trading in Pakistan and India). Anyone who promises a fixed daily profit is the biggest red flag (read the truth about signal groups).

How long does it take to learn forex?

There is no single answer, because everyone learns at a different speed. Some people understand the basics in two weeks, others take two months, and both are fine. One rule: move to the next lesson only when the previous lesson's idea is clear and its practical task is done. New lessons are added every day. After the basics, the next step is the free Price Action Mastery course.

Today's practical task (10 minutes)

Take a notebook and write three things:

  1. Why do I want to learn forex?
  2. How much time can I give every day?
  3. What is the most money I could lose without it affecting my life?

Answer honestly, and never put household money, loans or borrowed money at risk. Then look through the complete syllabus and start Lesson 1.1: What is forex trading?

lessons.notes:
Can $100 really make 10% a day?

You have probably seen the claim: invest $100 and earn 10% profit every day. Let's do the maths. If $100 grew by 10% a day and you reinvested the profit every day, after 30 days it would be about $1,744.94. After a full year the number would be bigger than all the personal wealth in the world. This is only a maths illustration, not a possible trading result. If it were that easy, everyone would be rich. So how is money really made in forex, and how is it lost?

Who is in the forex market?

About $9.6 trillion of currency changes hands every day (BIS Triennial Survey 2025). Six kinds of players share that market:

PlayerWho they areWhy they trade
Big banksThe heart of the market. They quote buy and sell prices all day.Profit from the spread and their own trading
Central banksFor example the State Bank of Pakistan or the Bank of Japan.Manage their own currency, not profit
Big institutionsHedge funds, investment funds and smaller banks; roughly half of all trading.Profit
Import and export companiesBuy and sell currency to pay for goods.Protect their business (hedging), not profit
Brokers and liquidity providersConnect ordinary traders to the big market.Spread, commission, swap, and sometimes your loss
Retail traders (us)Only a few percent of the whole market.Profit, but we are the smallest fish

How powerful is a central bank? On 15 January 2015 the Swiss National Bank removed its cap on the franc with one announcement. Within minutes the Swiss franc jumped about 30%. Many retail accounts were wiped out in a single day, and a London broker went bankrupt. Retail traders like us are the smallest fish in this ocean, which is why we learn to protect ourselves first.

How to earn money from forex trading: where profit comes from

In forex, money is made from the price difference. You buy EUR/USD and the price goes up: profit. It goes down: loss. If you sell, it is the opposite. (Lesson 1.1: What is forex trading? explains buy and sell from zero.)

On the other side of every trade there is someone: another trader, a bank or liquidity provider, or your own broker. One single person does not lose exactly what you win every time, but across the whole market money is not created out of thin air; it moves from one hand to another. So a winner's money comes from two places:

  1. The losses of traders who lose.
  2. Players who trade for their needs, not for profit, such as companies and central banks.

Your profit is not a gift from the market. It came out of someone's pocket, so to win you must make better decisions than others.

Where losers' money goes: 4 places

Where it goesHowRead more
1. Fees: spread, commission, swapThe spread puts every trade slightly in minus the moment it opens. Commission applies on some account types. Swap is charged (or sometimes paid) for holding a trade overnight.What is spread · What is swap
2. The broker itselfMany brokers do not send every trade to the big market; they take the other side themselves (often called a B-book). Then your loss becomes the broker's profit. This does not mean every broker cheats, but you should know it.Forex brokers guide
3. Better traders and institutionsBanks, funds and disciplined traders with better information, tools and risk control.Risk management
4. Outside the market: scams and signal sellersPaid signal groups, account managers and "guaranteed profit" schemes take money before a single trade is placed.Signal groups · Is forex a scam?

Islamic (swap-free) accounts

Many brokers offer an Islamic or swap-free account with no swap. But most of them charge a fixed admin fee for holding a trade overnight, either after a few days or from the first day. Some widen the spread a little, and some charge no admin fee at all. Not every broker works the same way, so read your broker's terms before opening an account. Module 4 covers broker and account types in detail.

Why the total is negative (the shovel sellers)

A fee is cut on every trade. So if you add up the profit and loss of all traders, the total is not zero: it is minus. Think of a cake where one slice is always cut away as a fee before anyone eats. The people who earn whether the market goes up or down are brokers, banks and signal sellers. In a gold rush, the one who earns most is the one selling shovels.

That is why regulated brokers in Europe and the UK must publish a risk warning on their own websites, and those warnings typically say about 60% to 80% of their retail accounts lose money trading CFDs.

The truth about a $50 or $100 account

Say you risk 2% of your account on each trade. On $100 that is $2, on $50 just $1. If a good trader makes 5% in a whole month, which is a very good result and not guaranteed, that is $5 on $100 and $2.50 on $50.

AccountRisk per tradeMost you lose on one tradeA very good month (+5%)
$502%$1.00$2.50
$1002%$2.00$5.00
$5003%$15.00$25.00
$1,0001%$10.00$50.00
$10,0001%$100.00$500.00

Can this run a household? No. This is where people go wrong: $5 feels too small, so they put 20% or 30% on one trade, and a few trades later the account is gone. A small account is for learning, not for earning.

How much should you risk per trade?

Risk means: if this trade goes wrong, how much of your account goes. You control it with a stop loss and the right lot size (Module 8 covers it fully; you can already try the free lot size calculator). A practical rule:

  • Small account ($50–$500): 2–3% per trade is acceptable, because the amount is small anyway and it is a learning account.
  • Bigger account: 1% or less, because every percent is now a big amount. 1% of $10,000 is $100.

10 losing trades in a row: 1% vs 3% vs 20% risk

Ten losses in a row can happen to any trader. Here is what it does to the account:

Risk per tradeAccount after 10 lossesTotal drawdown
1%$904.38−9.6%
3%$737.42−26.3%
20%$107.37−89.3%

At 1% you can recover. At 20% the account is practically finished (read more about drawdown and recovery).

Is forex trading profitable?

Yes, but only for traders who manage risk. That means three things: before every trade you decide the most you can lose, you have a daily and weekly loss limit, and you trade a tested plan. In the market, the one who earns is the one who survives first. Protect first, then earn.

Today's practical task (10 minutes)

  1. Open your broker's website and find the line that says what percentage of retail accounts lose money.
  2. Write down your account amount and work out 1% and 3% of it.

Write your answer in the YouTube comments. Next lesson: the biggest traps in the forex world, scams, signal groups and guaranteed-profit promises, and how to spot them from far away. If you missed it, start with Lesson 0.1: the course roadmap, or see the full syllabus.

Lekin fees ki wajah se sab traders ka total minus hai, is liye sirf woh kamata hai jo har trade par risk fix rakhe (chhote account par 2-3%, bare par 1% ya kam), daily aur weekly limit rakhe aur tested plan par trade kare. Pehle bachao, phir kamao.
How do you make money from forex trading?

From the price difference: you buy a pair and it rises, or sell and it falls. The money comes from the losses of other traders and from players who trade for their needs, such as companies and central banks. After fees the total of all traders is negative, so only traders with better decisions and strict risk control end up in profit.
Is forex trading profitable?

It can be, but most retail traders lose. Regulated brokers' own risk warnings typically say about 60% to 80% of retail CFD accounts lose money. Profit is possible only with a tested plan, a fixed risk per trade and daily and weekly loss limits.
Can I make money in forex with $100?
You can learn with $100, but not earn a living. At 2% risk you lose at most $2 per trade, and a very good month of +5% is about $5. A small account is a learning account.
Where does the money lost in forex go?

To four places: fees (spread, commission and swap), the broker itself when it takes the other side of your trade, better traders and institutions, and, outside the market, scams and paid signal sellers.
How much should I risk per trade?

On a small learning account of about $50 to $500, 2–3% per trade is acceptable. On a bigger account keep it at 1% or less. After 10 losses in a row, 1% risk costs about 9.6% of the account, 20% risk costs about 89%.
Is forex a zero-sum game?

Before costs, roughly yes: money moves from one hand to another. After the spread, commission and swap are taken out, the total of all traders is negative, which is why brokers, banks and signal sellers earn whichever way the market moves.
Do Islamic swap-free accounts have no cost?

They have no swap, but most brokers charge a fixed admin fee for holding trades overnight, either after a few days or from the first day, and some widen the spread. Terms differ, so read your broker's conditions.

lessons.notes:
What is forex?

Forex comes from two English words: foreign and exchange. It means changing the currency of one country into the currency of another. When someone in Pakistan buys US dollars, when a company in India buys euros to import a machine from Europe, or when a tourist changes money into dirhams in Dubai, that is forex.

Forex trading means buying or selling a currency with the aim of profiting from a change in its price.

How big is the forex market?

According to the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Triennial Survey, about $9.6 trillion worth of currencies changed hands every day in April 2025. That is why forex is called the largest financial market in the world. It has no single building: banks and institutions around the world are linked by computers, and the market runs 24 hours a day, five days a week (see the market timings in Pakistan and India).

A simple example: the money changer

Ahmed buys 100 US dollars from a money changer at Rs 280 per dollar and pays Rs 28,000. A few days later the dollar rises to Rs 285. He sells the same 100 dollars and receives Rs 28,500: a profit of Rs 500.

If the dollar had fallen to Rs 276, he would have received Rs 27,600: a loss of Rs 400. This is the whole idea behind forex trading: profit or loss from the difference in price. (The numbers are only an example.)

Rate100 USD in rupeesResult
BuyRs 280Rs 28,000-
Sell if the dollar risesRs 285Rs 28,500+Rs 500
Sell if the dollar fallsRs 276Rs 27,600-Rs 400

Why do currency prices change?

Because of demand and supply. When many people and companies want dollars and there are few dollars available, the dollar becomes expensive. When there are plenty of dollars and few buyers, it becomes cheaper. Demand is moved by interest rates, inflation, economic news and world events. Each of these gets its own lesson later in the series.

How online forex trading works

Today most forex trading happens online. You do not hold the dollars in your hand: through a broker, on a platform such as MT5 on your computer or phone, you trade on the price going up or down.

  • Currencies are always quoted in pairs, for example the euro against the US dollar, written EUR/USD.
  • If EUR/USD rises from 1.1000 to 1.1050, the euro has become stronger against the dollar.
  • Not only currencies: Gold is traded too, as XAU/USD.
  • Pips, lots and spread come in the next lessons.

The honest truth about risk

Forex is not a job and not a get-rich-quick scheme. Price differences make losses just as easily as profits. Many regulated brokers state on their own websites that most of their retail clients' accounts lose money. The usual reason is trading without learning, without a plan and with too much risk. Anyone who promises "guaranteed profit" or "fixed daily income" is showing the biggest red flag (read about signal scams).

Is forex trading legal?

The rules are different in every country. In India, for example, the Reserve Bank of India allows residents to trade forex only through authorised persons and on recognised exchanges, for permitted purposes. Before you start anything, check the official rules of your own country. Our guide to forex trading in Pakistan and India explains the details.

The most common beginner mistake

Watching two videos, or taking someone's signal, and putting real money in on the first day. The right path is: learn first, practise on a demo account, make your own plan, then start small. This whole series follows that path.

Practical task (10 minutes)

  1. Note today's US dollar rate in rupees from a bank's website. Check it again after three days and write down who gained from the change: the person who bought dollars or the person who sold them?
  2. Write one line: "Why do I want to learn forex?" Share your answer in the YouTube comments.

Learn first, practise on demo, make your plan, and only then start with small money.

faq: Forex trading kya hai?

Forex trading ek currency ko doosri currency ke muqable mein khareedna ya bechna hai, taa ke qeemat badalne se faida ho. Misal: dollar Rs 280 par khareed kar Rs 285 par bechna. Forex market banks, companies aur traders ka duniya bhar ka currency market hai jo hafte mein 5 din, 24 ghante khula rehta hai.
What is forex trading in simple words?
Forex trading is buying or selling one currency against another to profit from a change in its price, for example buying US dollars at Rs 280 and selling them at Rs 285.
How does the forex market work?
Banks, companies, institutions and individual traders exchange currencies through a worldwide computer network, 24 hours a day, five days a week. Prices move with demand and supply.
How big is the forex market?
According to the BIS Triennial Survey, average daily forex turnover was about $9.6 trillion in April 2025, which makes it the largest financial market in the world.
Can you lose money in forex trading?
Yes. The same price change that gives one trader a profit gives another a loss. Many regulated brokers state that most of their retail clients lose money. Learn first and practise on a demo account.
Is forex trading legal in Pakistan and India?

The rules depend on the country. In India the RBI allows residents to trade forex only through authorised persons and recognised exchanges for permitted purposes. Always check your own country's official rules.
How do I start forex trading as a beginner?
Learn the basics in order (this free series), open a demo account, practise with a written plan and small risk, and only then think about a small real account.
